question: Can compact activation vectors localized by causal mediation carry visual relations in large multimodal models, improve relation prediction without demonstrations, and compose into unseen spatial relations?

key_findings.claim: The paper localizes relation-sensitive computation to a sparse group of intermediate-layer attention heads and constructs one function vector per relation from their task-conditioned activations.
key_findings.evidence: For each relation, the authors compare clean and perturbed in-context prompts, rank every head by average indirect effect, retain the ten highest-scoring heads, and average their last-token activations. The head-count ablation peaks around 6-12 heads and then degrades, while middle-layer injection is strongest.

key_findings.claim: Fine-tuning only the injected vector can outperform both the unmodified model and few-shot prompting on held-out relation tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Model parameters remain frozen while one vector is optimized on a dedicated training split. Figure 6 reports the fine-tuned vector as the strongest of zero-shot, four-shot ICL, initial-vector, and fine-tuned-vector conditions across the synthetic and GQA aggregates; on ten unseen synthetic objects it reaches 13.6% versus 9.4% ICL for OpenFlamingo and 72.2% versus 21.3% ICL for Qwen3-VL.

key_findings.claim: A weighted combination of four base spatial vectors improves one-shot analogies for diagonal relations absent from training.
key_findings.evidence: The source analogy determines weights over above, below, left, and right vectors; the composed vector is then injected for the target without retaining demonstrations. Accuracy rises from the strongest reported four-shot ICL baseline of 8.1% to 16.8% on OpenFlamingo and from 28.7% to 45.1% on Qwen3-VL over 1,000 above-left/right and below-left/right tasks.

key_findings.claim: The causal language is stronger than the intervention design can fully support: patching identifies components sufficient to change answers under this prompt family, not a unique or complete relational circuit.
key_findings.evidence: Average indirect effect is computed from a particular clean-versus-perturbed contrast, the vector aggregates multiple heads, and the paper reports that performance eventually falls as more heads are included. It does not test redundant circuits, necessity via ablation, counterfactual image edits, or whether the intervention changes relation knowledge rather than downstream answer-token preferences.

key_findings.claim: The claimed compositional generalization remains a controlled proof of concept rather than evidence for broad visual-relation algebra.
key_findings.evidence: Only four diagonal relations are synthesized from the same four axis-aligned bases; mixture weights require a source example, so the setting is explicitly one-shot rather than zero-shot. The authors also acknowledge narrow spatial/agentic categories and contextual-demonstration dependence.

method.core_idea: Extend language-model function vectors to visual relations by causally ranking multimodal-model attention heads, averaging the most influential activations into a relation vector, and injecting or optimizing that vector at inference time.
method.mechanism: Four-shot relation prompts provide clean task activations; label- or context-perturbed prompts provide a contrast. Average indirect effects rank language-module attention heads. The top ten activations are averaged per relation and added at a selected middle layer in zero-shot prompts. A frozen-model training stage updates only the vector. For unseen diagonal relations, a source analogy estimates weights used to linearly combine four learned base-relation vectors.
assumptions: A clean-versus-perturbed prompt contrast isolates relation execution rather than unrelated prompt or label effects.
The last-token activation of a small attention-head subset is a faithful carrier of relational information.
Additive activation intervention preserves enough of the model's native computation to interpret accuracy changes mechanistically.
Synthetic layouts and filtered GQA relations represent the kinds of relation reasoning relevant to broader multimodal use.
Linear combinations of axis-aligned relation vectors meaningfully approximate composite relations.
Object-disjoint examples and relation-disjoint diagonals are sufficient tests against memorization and leakage.

techniques.role: Ranks attention heads by the clean-to-perturbed indirect effect on relation answers.
Averages selected last-token head activations into a compact relation-specific intervention.
Optimizes only the injected vector on held-out relation examples while freezing the LMM.
Combines base relation vectors using weights inferred from a source analogy.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic four-relation images and GQA spatial/agentic subsets
evaluations.result: Fine-tuned vectors lead the four evaluated inference conditions in the reported aggregates.
evaluations.baseline: Zero-shot, one-/four-shot ICL, and the initial untuned function vector.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic object-disjoint test with ten unseen objects
evaluations.result: 13.6% for OpenFlamingo and 72.2% for Qwen3-VL with fine-tuned vectors.
evaluations.baseline: OpenFlamingo ICL 9.4%/initial vector 11.0%; Qwen3-VL ICL 21.3%/initial vector 23.3%.

evaluations.result: Composite vectors reach 16.8% on OpenFlamingo and 45.1% on Qwen3-VL.
evaluations.baseline: Best displayed four-shot ICL values of 8.1% and 28.7%, respectively.

limitations: Only two 4B-class models are studied, and architecture-specific head locations do not agree across them.
The relation inventory is narrow: four synthetic spatial, seven GQA spatial, and five GQA agentic labels.
The paper provides aggregate plots without seed-level uncertainty, confidence intervals, or multiple-run robustness for vector optimization.
Causal mediation uses a single intervention family and does not establish a minimal, necessary, or unique circuit.
Fine-tuned-vector comparisons do not match the training-data or optimization budget of parameter-efficient adaptation baselines.
Composite vectors require one labeled source analogy and are tested only on diagonals constructed from the trained axes.
Absolute OpenFlamingo accuracies remain low even after intervention, despite favorable relative improvements.
No specificity audit measures collateral changes to object identity, language fluency, unrelated relations, or calibration.
failure_modes: Head rankings may change under paraphrased prompts, different answer vocabularies, image order, or model checkpoints.
Activation addition can directly bias answer tokens without improving visual grounding or procedural relation reasoning.
A tuned vector can encode dataset-specific object or scene regularities despite object-disjoint synthetic evaluation.
Linear composition may fail for asymmetric, non-spatial, social, temporal, or higher-arity relations.
Large injection magnitudes can overwrite rather than steer native computation, while small magnitudes may not transfer across layers or models.
Source-derived mixture weights can leak the target relation definition, making the analogy easier than naturally occurring transfer.
reusable_insights: Pair localization claims with both necessity and sufficiency interventions; clean-to-corrupt patching alone supports only a bounded causal claim.
Head-count and injection-layer sweeps are essential because mechanistic interventions can have a narrow effective operating region.
Object-disjoint and relation-disjoint splits test different generalization axes and should both be reported.
Activation vectors can be treated as lightweight trainable modules, but their data and optimization budget should be compared to adapters or soft prompts.
Compositional-vector claims become stronger when mixture coefficients are preregistered and evaluated on nontrivial algebraic relations, not only geometric diagonals.
open_questions: Do the selected heads remain causally important under image counterfactuals that preserve objects but change only the relation?
Can necessity ablations and distributed-pathway searches distinguish a sparse carrier from redundant relational circuits?
How stable are vectors across seeds, prompts, layers, model scales, and architectural families?
Does vector tuning beat LoRA, adapters, soft prompts, and linear probes under equal data, parameters, and compute?
Can relation vectors compose for depth, containment, temporal, social, transitive, or ternary relations with predictable algebra?
What diagnostics separate improved grounding from answer-token steering?
Can a zero-shot router infer composition weights without a source analogy?

competitive_landscape.title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct language-only methodological predecessor for causal-mediation localization and activation-vector task execution.
competitive_landscape.difference: Todd et al. establish compact function vectors across language tasks and models, including limited vector composition. The reviewed work transfers that recipe to visual relations, adds frozen-vector tuning, and tests two LMMs; it therefore extends rather than originates the core mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Visual Task Vectors
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct visual task-vector predecessor in a visual-prompting model.
competitive_landscape.difference: Finding Visual Task Vectors averages intermediate activations and uses REINFORCE to select task vectors for example-free task guidance in MAE-VQGAN. The reviewed work operates in interleaved LMMs, ranks heads by causal mediation, and targets named object relations and analogy composition.

competitive_landscape.title: Multimodal Task Vectors Enable Many-Shot Multimodal In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest multimodal activation-compression competitor and cited predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Multimodal Task Vectors compress many demonstrations to escape context-length limits and test task/OOD transfer. The reviewed method instead isolates relation-specific causal heads, tunes the resulting vector, and studies compositional analogies, but evaluates fewer models and a narrower behavior family.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Probing for Internal Visual Representations in Multimodal Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current causal activation-steering analysis of visual concepts and visual reasoning in MLLMs.
competitive_landscape.difference: Causal Probing compares localization across visual concept types and reports that abstract concepts are distributed and that recognized geometry need not trigger procedural reasoning. This directly sharpens the reviewed paper's sparse-localization interpretation and motivates tests separating relation perception, storage, and execution.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim the first systematic extraction, causal manipulation, tuning, and linear composition of visual-relation function vectors in large multimodal models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The full text demonstrates the pipeline on OpenFlamingo-4B and Qwen3-VL-4B, controlled synthetic and GQA relations, object-disjoint tests, and four held-out diagonal relations. Primary-source comparison confirms that function vectors, visual task vectors, and multimodal task vectors predate this work.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is relation-specific multimodal causal localization plus vector-only tuning and one-shot diagonal composition in a single framework. The core activation-vector mechanism is inherited, causal completeness is not established, and general compositionality remains unproven beyond a narrow controlled construction.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text pass over all 18 extracted pages, including appendices and the reported ablations. Numerical values are author-reported from the paper; causal-scope, comparison-budget, and compositional-generalization qualifications are reviewer inferences. Four primary arXiv records were checked on 2026-08-23. No independent rerun, code audit, or secondary verification is claimed.
